name: One deployable on the person's Windows machine, a module per domain

groups.name: Policy Definitions
groups.note: The catalogue of policy definitions a person can browse: categories, products, support rules and policies, and the text they are shown in.

groups.name: Policy Source
groups.note: Where policy settings and their comments are kept, how a place is opened, remembered, checked for writability and released.

groups.name: Policy State
groups.note: Whether a policy is on, off or unset in an area, and the change of that state with its options and comment.

groups.name: Policy Discovery
groups.note: Finding the policy a person has in mind by name, words, setting or filter and reviewing what was found.

groups.name: Policy File Exchange
groups.note: Direct work on the raw keys and values of a stored policy and the exchange of whole policy files.

groups.name: Definition Acquisition
groups.note: Getting Microsoft's current policy definitions installed where the program can use them.

groups.name: Workspace
groups.note: The person's working session: which definitions are loaded and from where, the language, what is remembered between visits, what is shown about the program and what is let go.

boxes.note: Walks a person through getting the current definitions installed, reports which stage failed and hands the resulting folder over for loading.
Decides whether missing definitions should be offered to the person, from the share of non-empty categories that name a missing parent.
Finds the template files in a chosen folder and ignores everything else; reads them through the outside parser.
Reads template and language files from a folder and gives back their parsed documents.
Chooses the language text file for each template: exact language, same family, then English.
Reads a language file and refuses flawed ones; resolves text references into shown text.
Remembers the person's language for definition text and offers to reload at once.
Reads and validates each template, refuses or skips unsound ones and stops on a missing namespace.
Builds categories, products, support rules and policies from the validated templates and joins them to the available set.
Reads each policy option and its entry layout, with defaults and storage effects.
Works out whether a support definition is met for chosen products.
Runs a load from folder or single files, replaces or adds, reports problems and remembers the folder.
Empties the loaded definitions at once and restores them on request.
Works out each policy's state and comment for the shown area or both, with filters.
Presents the category tree with visibility, icons, selection and area choice.
Lists the chosen category and shows the description of the focused item.
Decides which actions fit the item and takes it as focus before acting.
Finds identical user and computer pairs and merges them after confirmation.
Shows a policy's section, place and support with gaps flagged.
Shows a category with its chain of parents and policies.
Lists products with child counts and shows versions and details.
Filters support definitions and shows entries, with the products covered.
Gives a plain summary of a policy first and presentation and element detail on demand.
Writes a policy in the semantic text form per area.
Lists loaded files with what each defines.
Resolves an identifier to a policy, category, product or support definition and opens it.
Turns policy file bytes into entries and entries back into bytes: signature and version, text and number encodings, ordering and duplicate handling.
Holds the entries of one policy file in memory and answers presence, reading, setting, forgetting, deletion marking and key clearing.
Reads, writes, deletes and clears the live policy keys of the machine, checks root names and tests whether the keys can be written.
Loads a user's stored settings file into the machine registry under a temporary name and unloads it when the source is released.
Holds settings destined for an exported registry text file: branch-limited saving, deleting and clearing, and a refusal for every read or check.
Applies the changes of one policy file onto another source, including marker-style entries and the forgetting of dropped values.
An empty in-memory policy store that can be changed and is never saved.
Reads and writes policy files and their folders on the machine, creating missing policy files empty and opening them for reading and writing.
Creates and raises the version file that sits beside a policy file so the machine notices a change.
Works out where a source's policy file and comment file live from its kind and the detail given.
Names each source, decides whether it is fully writable, can only be viewed or lives in memory, and words the readiness notice after opening.
Closes the sources already open, opens the user and computer sources from a choice or from the default, and falls back when one cannot be opened.
Releases each open source on leaving and tells the person when resources are still held elsewhere.
Remembers the chosen kinds and details of both sources and offers them again, replacing them with the defaults when they cannot be reached.
Saves comments, then each fully writable source by its kind, refreshes or applies the change, remembers the sources and reports one line per source.
Keeps the comments of each source by policy and area, finds them when a comment is wanted and saves the whole list to the comment file location.
Reads and writes the comment files beside policy sources: validates their definitions and gives each comment its own text id and prefix.
Turns a typed user name into the account's security identifier through the directory and checks that an identifier is valid.
Creates the user and computer sources from the chosen kind and detail, naming which side failed and why.
Decides which details are open for the kind chosen, which files are accepted and how leaving without choosing ends.
Ends the naming of a user without a choice when the person leaves.
Proposes the person's own profile, lists the others and returns the settings file path only once a profile is chosen.
After sources open or a view setting changes, moves to the nearest visible category and drops a selection that is no longer shown.
Counts enabled and disabled evidence from the values and lists a source holds for a policy and its options, and settles the policy's state in an area.
Reads the stored value of each option of a policy from a source: numbers, text, choices, ticks and lists.
Finds every value a policy touches and clears them, with key clearances, from a source.
Writes the chosen state of a policy with its own on and off values and its options into a source.
Saves one option's value under the right key with the right kind of value.
Stores, replaces or removes a policy's comment and says when a source holds no comments.
Holds one open edit of a policy: the area, the writable check, the chosen state, the forecast, and how it ends as a change or a cancel.
Decides what each option control accepts, starts with and offers.
Reads semantic policy text into policies, states and settings, and reports what is wrong and on which line.
Applies read policies to the right source, skipping and counting the ones that fail, and reports the outcome.
Holds the text being brought in, from a file or typed, and offers apply only for text that read correctly.
Writes a policy's settings as semantic policy text, with or without the heading.
Gives the state of each policy in an area, and of the sources being worked on, to the screens that show them, by reading it through the evidence reader and returning it as plain facts.
Decides whether a policy is listed, from the chosen area and, when the filter is on, from every active part of the limit: type, state, comment and products.
Offers exactly three area choices and starts on the first, so both areas are shown at the start.
Trims the typed identifier, cuts off a section suffix and looks the kind up in the fixed order, policy last.
Opens what was found as its kind requires, says when nothing is found, and shows the matching icon.
Keeps at most one item of the policy list selected.
Splits the typed words into plain words, wildcard words and quoted phrases, cleaned of punctuation, dropping a phrase never closed.
Decides whether a text holds every word, wildcard and phrase, and whether a policy hits through its title, description or comments.
Accepts the typed words and the chosen places, refusing empty words or no place, and starts the search for both areas.
Works out which part of a pasted line is the key and which the value, so the reading can be shown and corrected.
Judges at once whether the typed terms are usable, refusing empty terms and a root key, and starts the search when usable.
Decides whether one setting a policy reads or writes meets the key and value terms with wildcard, prefix, whole-name and path-part rules.
Runs a search over every policy in order, adds hits with their category, reports progress every twenty policies, supports cancelling and reports how it ended.
Accepts only a chosen hit, remembers its position and opens that policy's editor in the current area.
Takes the next hit still shown after the last one chosen, says when none is left, and returns nothing when no search ran.
Holds the last results and chosen position, reopens them without a new search, and forgets them when the search is cleared.
Shows the limit in force as editable choices: type, state, comment and products, with the defaults when a condition is absent.
Turns the chosen type, state, comment and products into the new limit's conditions.
Opens product choice only while a support limit is wanted and spreads a hand choice to the products beneath.
Switches the limit on or off and moves to the nearest category still shown.
Returns every choice to its default and, when the round is abandoned, puts back the limit held at the start.

Decides whether raw editing may start: limits the area to sources backed by a policy file, tells the person plainly when none is, asks only when both are, and shows the caution to a person who has not accepted it, remembering a yes and asking again after a no.
Lists the file's keys and values as an ordered tree, each key once ignoring case, with each value's content and the special deletion entries named as such.
Works out which actions fit the current selection: nothing, a key, an ordinary value or a deletion entry.
Summarises the changes made in the session, reminds that they reach disk only on saving, and keeps them however editing is left.
Checks a typed key name as it is typed: refuses a backslash or a name already used under the same parent ignoring case, and treats an empty name or a back-out as adding nothing.
Adds the empty key under the selected key or at the top level and selects it.
Takes a value's name and data together, starts on string, suggests the kind from the data, sets starting data by kind, and stores only on confirmation, replacing a same-named value.
Reads typed numbers as decimal or marked hexadecimal and limits them to the 32-bit or 64-bit range.
Shows a value's current data in the form fitting its kind, refuses unsupported kinds, and replaces the data keeping name and kind and the value selected.
Replaces a selected value with a deletion entry named from the value, so it is removed on the machine when policies are applied.
Offers clear everything, clear while keeping existing ordinary direct values, or delete one value by typed name; accepts no choice by default and refuses an empty name.
Describes what will go, asks for confirmation, and removes a key with its contents or a value with its deletion entry, leaving nothing behind.
Accepts only exported-settings files, remembers the chosen source, refuses a missing file or prefix, warns about default values, and leaves without change on a back-out.
Checks the file is a genuine export and reads keys, removals, deletions, default values and typed data, skipping blank and comment lines.
Works out the key prefix from the first key of the file, and warns while leaving it empty when that fails.
Applies the read settings to the chosen source: clears removed keys, deletes marked values, saves the rest with the prefix removed, reports only failure, then refreshes the view.
Reads a policy file and applies it to the chosen source as the difference from an empty file, reporting a file that cannot be loaded and changing nothing; the result is held until saved.
Chooses the starting branch and prefix of an export, trims a trailing backslash from a branch, and refuses an export without a file name.
Provides the policy file to export: a file-backed source as is, a registry-backed source rebuilt from the three policy locations with types kept.
Writes the chosen branch of the file as a settings script with removal and deletion marks, escaping and typed data, wrapped lines, and reports success or failure.
Writes the chosen area's policy source as a policy file and reports success or failure.

Runs one acquisition from start to result: locks the start, close and destination controls while it runs, refuses leaving mid-run, reports the failed step, re-enables everything, and after success asks whether to open the definitions and reports the folder only on yes.

Proposes the operating system's policy definitions folder each time an acquisition opens, reports no new folder, and replaces the destination with a chosen folder while a cancelled choice changes nothing.
Downloads the one fixed Microsoft package into a scratch folder under local application data, allowing no version choice and only the permitted secure protocols.
Unpacks the downloaded package with the operating system's installer tool, stops on a failure keeping the package, and deletes the package on success.

Takes ownership and gives Administrators full control of an existing destination before any move for administrators, and resets ownership and inherited permissions on folders and moved files; standard users change nothing.

Replaces files in the destination with the templates, then the language files of the regional format language, and the English fallback when that language is not English (United States), creating folders and deleting same-named files first.
Asks the operating system for its edition and decides from a fixed list of codes whether Group Policy infrastructure exists, treating a failed query as none.

Decides whether to offer the definitions once the edition lacks Group Policy and more than two non-empty categories name a missing parent, shows the welcome question, and starts an acquisition on yes.
After a successful acquisition, empties the workspace, loads the acquired folder, saves it as the definitions folder and rebuilds the view; with no new folder nothing changes.

At build time derives the program version from the source history (tag, commit count and short commit name, or a short commit name) and writes it into the generated version source; the committed source keeps an empty version.
Provides the author, the project address and the version only when one was built in.
Reads and writes named preference rows in the preference store; when the store cannot be reached it yields defaults, drops changes and does not alert the person.
Gives typed access to the remembered choices (chosen sources, definitions folder, language, caution accepted, offer considered) over the preference adapter, for the other parts of the workspace.
Decides which definitions folder to load at start: the last saved one, else the system default folder.

Loads the saved definitions at session start and handles trouble: asks whether to keep a partly loaded set, discards it on refusal, offers the default location for a failed non-default folder, saves the default on acceptance, and reports a failed default load leaving the set empty.

Offers the standard folder, the domain folder only when joined to a domain and present, or a typed folder; makes the typed folder usable only when chosen; refuses a missing folder; treats cancellation as no choice.
Proposes replacing the loaded definitions by default, asks only when something is loaded, and passes the choice on only for an accepted existing folder.
Empties the set first only when replacing, adds the folder reporting problems without stopping, reports a failed addition with its reason, and remembers the folder only after a successful replace.
Accepts one or several template files only and adds them to the current set without emptying it or remembering a folder; reports a failure with its reason.
Empties the loaded definitions and previous search results at once, without confirmation, whenever the set is closed or replaced, and rebuilds what is shown.
Accepts a language code only when it has exactly two parts around a hyphen, otherwise refuses it plainly; treats a code equal to the stored one as no change.
Saves the new language code at once, asks whether to reload now, and on yes empties the set and reloads from the saved folder.
Records on first start that the welcome offer was considered, even if none is made, and never considers it again; keeps a standing invitation to get definitions.
Takes the staged definitions as the ones in use: empties the set, adds them, and remembers the folder; does nothing without a new folder.
